source.subject: defer qwatch tokens and skip dedicated servers

answers.question: Where do my Quake game files go?
answers.answer:
Put them in the `id1` folder inside your Quake base directory. The base directory is the folder holding the engine and all game directories [1], and the game looks for files starting in `id1/` [2].

- To see the exact paths in use, type `path` [2].
- To point the engine at a different base directory, launch it with `-basedir "c:\quake"` [1].
- Mods live in their own game directory; load one with `game` (or `gamedir`) [3].
- To list files, use `dir` with wildcards, e.g. `dir *.pak` [4].

`.pak` files also count as path locations, since they contain directory information [2].

answers.question: Where are my settings saved, and how do I use an autoexec.cfg?
answers.answer:
Your settings are saved in `config.cfg` [1]. QSS-M autosaves on quit, but a crash can lose changes, so use `writeconfig` to save immediately; you can also pass a filename to save a new config [1]. `resetcfg` resets only cvars that save to the config back to defaults [2]. `cfg_save_aliases` defaults to `1`, saving non-server aliases to config.cfg [3]; `cfg_unbindall` defaults to `1`, clearing binds before stored bindings load [4].

An autoexec.cfg is a console script: put commands in it, one per line; lines starting `//` are comments. Load it with `exec autoexec.cfg` [5]. Scripts can use any extension, but `.cfg` and `.rc` are common; use a path relative to the current directory, usually `quake/id1/`, not an absolute path [5]. To run it at startup, set `cl_onload "exec autoexec.cfg"`; cl_onload accepts any valid command that takes arguments [6]. autoexec.cfg is one of the config files [7].

answers.question: How do I run a mod or mission pack?
answers.answer:
To load a mod while playing, type `game <modname>` in the console; `gamedir <modname>` does the same thing [1]. To start directly into a mod, add `-game <modname>` to the launch command [2].

For mission packs, launch QSS-M with one of these command-line options:
- `-hipnotic` [3]
- `-rogue` [4]
- `-quoth` [5]

Only one mission-pack option should be specified [3][5][4].

In cooperative games, a server can enable mod voting with `sv_modvote 1` (default `0`); eligible players then use `modvote` to switch to a selected installed mod [6].

answers.question: How do I download and play custom maps?
answers.answer:
Set your web download URLs, then fetch the map and load it.

- `cl_web_download_url` defaults to `q1tools/q1tools.github.io` and `cl_web_download_url2` defaults to `maps.quakeworld.nu` [1][2]. Web downloads are much faster than pulling files from the server; if both are blank, QSS-M only tries the connected server [1][2].
- Type `download aerowalk.bsp` to fetch a map. The same command also handles `.lit`, `.wav`, and `.loc` files, and `download ctf` or `download ra` grabs the client files for those mods [3].
- Then load it with `map aerowalk` [4]. On a server, `map` disconnects all players first, so use `changelevel` instead when changing maps on a game server [4].
- To find a map, run `maps` for a list with worldspawn descriptions, or `maps chamber` to search all maps [5].

Extra maps can also be placed in `id1/maps/` [4].

answers.question: How do I reset everything back to the defaults?
answers.answer:
Type `resetall` to reset every console variable to its engine default [1][2]. Use `resetcfg` instead if you only want the settings that are saved to config.cfg reset [3].

For a single variable, use `reset` followed by its name, e.g. `reset fov` — that restores the engine default [4].

- `resetall` — all cvars
- `resetcfg` — only cvars that save to the config
- `reset <cvar>` — one cvar

Settings autosave when you quit, but a crash would lose them; run `writeconfig` to save immediately [5].

answers.question: How do I change my field of view?
answers.answer:
Type `fov` followed by a number in the console. For example, `fov 110` widens your view. The default is `90`, and values are clamped between 10 and 170 [1].

- `fov_adapt` defaults to `1` and automatically scales your FOV for widescreen resolutions, so you see more to the sides instead of losing top and bottom [2]. Set `fov_adapt 0` to turn that off.
- `cl_gun_fovscale` defaults to `1` and compensates for weapon-model distortion when your FOV is above 90 [3]. You can adjust it with values above or below 1 to change the amount of distortion.

answers.question: How do I change resolution, fullscreen, and vsync?
answers.answer:
Type `vid_width` and `vid_height` to set the window/screen size, `vid_fullscreen` to switch between windowed and fullscreen, and `vid_vsync` to control vertical sync.

- `vid_width` — horizontal resolution, default `800` (cannot go below 320 in windowed mode) [1]
- `vid_height` — vertical resolution, default `600` (cannot go below 200 in windowed mode) [2]
- `vid_fullscreen` — set to `1` for fullscreen, `0` for a window; default `0` [3]
- `vid_vsync` — `1` enables vertical sync and caps your framerate at your monitor's refresh rate; `0` disables it and allows tearing; default `0` [4]

None of these take effect until you call `vid_restart` [3][2][1]. For a borderless window filling the screen, use `vid_desktopfullscreen 1` [5]. In fullscreen you can also set `vid_bpp` (`16` or `32`, default `16`) and `vid_refreshrate` (default `60`) [6][7]. To start fullscreen from the command line, add `-fullscreen`, or `-current` to start at your desktop resolution [8][9].

answers.question: How do I uncap or limit my framerate?
answers.answer:
Set `host_maxfps` to control your framerate. It defaults to `250`. Type `host_maxfps 0` for uncapped, or a positive number to cap it, e.g. `host_maxfps 144` [1]. This can also be changed from the video options menu [2].

To uncap rendering while keeping a fixed network send rate, use a negative value: `host_maxfps -72` runs uncapped but sends 72 packets per second [1]. This may slightly raise your displayed ping as a timing artifact [1].

`vid_vsync 1` enables vertical sync, which removes tearing but caps framerate at your monitor's refresh rate; it defaults to `0` [3].

To see your framerate, set `scr_showfps 1` (default `0`) [4].

answers.question: The game is too dark. How do I adjust brightness and gamma?
answers.answer:
Type `gamma 0.5` in the console to brighten the screen. The default is `1`; values below 1 are brighter, and values above 1 are darker [1]. `gamma` is saved to your config [1].

If raising gamma makes the image look gray or washed out, try `contrast` instead. Its default is `1`; raising it gives a richer image, but colors near white can clip to white [2]. `contrast` is also saved to your config [2].

If gamma changes don’t apply correctly, you can choose the gamma method on the command line:
- Add `-glslgamma` to prefer GLSL gamma correction [3].
- Add `-noglslgamma` to disable it [4].
- Add `-hwgamma` to prefer hardware gamma ramps [5].

For mapshots only, `cl_mapshots_brightness` defaults to `0.8` and dims them below `1` [6].

answers.question: How do I get the classic pixelated look, or smooth textures instead?
answers.answer:
For texture crispness, set the filtering mode with `gl_texturemode`.

- Pixelated, software-like: `gl_texturemode GL_NEAREST` (point sampled) [1]. `GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST` keeps distant textures slightly better while staying blocky [1].
- Smooth, highest quality: `gl_texturemode GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR` (trilinear) [1]. `gl_texturemode GL_LINEAR` gives no blending [1].
- Not sure of the names? Type `gl_describetexturemodes` to list them all [1][2].

For sharper distant surfaces, raise anisotropy: `gl_texture_anisotropy 4` (also 2, 8, 16); `1` is normal filtering [3].

Model skins are smoothed separately with `gl_smoothmodels 1`; set it to `0` to turn smoothing off [4].

For an overall low-resolution pixellated look, `r_scale 4` renders the view at 1/4 resolution (2 for 1/2, 3 for 1/3); the default is `1` [5].

answers.question: How do I hide or reposition the weapon model?
answers.answer:
Hide it with `r_drawviewmodel 0` (default `1`); it also accepts alpha values [1]. Set it back to `1` to show the weapon again.

To move the weapon model, use FTEQW-style offsets, all defaulting to `0` and clamped from -30 to 30 [2][3]:

- `cl_gunx` — positive moves right
- `cl_guny` — positive moves down
- `cl_gunz` — positive moves forward

For example, `cl_gunx 5` shifts the gun right, `cl_guny -5` shifts it up, and `cl_gunz 8` pushes it forward.

For the classic WinQuake gun position, set `r_viewmodel_quake 1` (default `0`) [4].

answers.question: How do I change my crosshair's style, color, and size?
answers.answer:
Set the crosshair type with `crosshair`: `0` is off (the default), `1` is white, `2` is colored, and values up to `7` give different options [1].

- Color: `scr_crosshaircolor` — default `0xffffff`; accepts HEX RGB or Quake colors `1`–`13` [2].
- Size: `scr_crosshairscale` — default `1`; `1` is normal, `10` is maximum enlargement [3].
- Opacity: `scr_crosshairalpha` — default `1` [4].

For example: `crosshair 2`, `scr_crosshaircolor 0x00ff00`, `scr_crosshairscale 2`.

If damage blinking is enabled, `scr_crosshaircshift` sets the color the crosshair changes to when you take damage; default `0xfc7303` [5].

answers.question: How do I change the HUD style and size?
answers.answer:
Use `scr_sbar` to choose the HUD style: `scr_sbar 1` for the default HUD, `scr_sbar 2` for QW style, or `scr_sbar 3` for the Quake re-release (QE) style. The default is `1` [1].

For size, use `scr_sbarscale`. `scr_sbarscale 1` draws at 1:1, while `scr_sbarscale 2` doubles it. Integer values look nicest. It won't draw smaller than 1:1 or larger than the window width. The default is `1` [2].

Both settings are saved to your config, so they persist between sessions.

answers.question: How do I show my FPS, ping, and a clock on screen?
answers.answer:
Type these in the console:

- `scr_showfps 1` — shows FPS. Default is `0` (off) [1].
- `scr_ping 1` — shows ping in milliseconds in the lower-left corner when connected. Default is already `1`; use `2` for ping without “ms”, or `3` for ping plus packet loss [2].
- `scr_clock 2` — shows a 12-hour system clock in the lower-right corner. Use `scr_clock 3` for a 24-hour clock with seconds, or `scr_clock 1` for level time. Default is `0` (off) [3].

All three are saved to your config, so they persist between sessions [1][3][2].

answers.question: How do I open the console and change its size or font scale?
answers.answer:
Press the tilde key (`~`) or type `toggleconsole` to lower or raise the console [1].

To change the console text size:

- `scr_conscale` scales the console text larger, but only has an effect when `scr_conwidth` is 0. Default is `1` [2].
- `scr_conwidth` sets the virtual console width, where smaller numbers mean larger text. Values below 320 or above the window width are clamped, and values are rounded to a multiple of 8. If 0, the window width is used. Default is `0` [3].
- `scr_consize` sets the vertical length of the console while the game is active; default is `.5`, or half the screen [4].

For an automatic fit, run `scr_autoscale`, which calculates a UI scale from your current resolution and applies it to the console, menus, status bar, and crosshair [5].

answers.question: How do I adjust mouse sensitivity or invert the mouse?
answers.answer:
Change overall mouse sensitivity with `sensitivity`; the default is `3` [1]. To keep a new value across restarts, use `seta` — for example, `seta sensitivity 5` [2].

- Invert vertical look: `seta m_pitch -0.022`. The default is `0.022`; a negative value reverses up/down mouse movement [3].
- Reverse horizontal turning: `seta m_yaw -0.022`. The default is `0.022`; a negative value reverses left/right mouse movement [4].
- For a controller’s look stick, `seta joy_invert 1` inverts the vertical axis; default is `0` [5].

On macOS, `in_disablemacosxmouseaccel` defaults to `2` and can affect game sensitivity [6].

answers.question: How do I bind keys and make aliases?
answers.answer:
Bind a command to a key with `bind <key> <command>`, e.g. `bind g "impulse 10"` [1]. For several commands on one key, wrap them in quotes and separate with semicolons: `bind x "+attack;+moveup"` [1]. Keys without printable characters (like the arrow keys) are bound by name, and ESCAPE or ~ can only be bound from an external config file [1].

To create an alias, use `alias <name> "<commands>"` [2]. Multiple commands separated by semicolons work inside an alias too. Typing `alias` alone prints every alias and its assignment, and `alias ready` shows just that one's string [2].

Manage them with:
- `bindlist` — list all key bindings [3]
- `unbind <key>` — remove one binding [4]
- `unbindall` — remove every binding except ESCAPE [5]
- `aliaslist` — alphabetized list of aliases [6]
- `unaliasall` — delete all aliases [7]

Aliases are saved to your config by default (`cfg_save_aliases` 1), and `cfg_unbindall` 1 clears old bindings before reloading them [8][9].

answers.question: How do I turn on mouse look and always run?
answers.answer:
Mouse look is controlled with `+mlook` to enable and `-mlook` to disable [1][2]. While it's active, moving the mouse forward and back makes you look up and down instead of moving, so `m_forward` has no effect [3].

Always run is the `cl_alwaysrun` variable, default `0`. Set it to 1 to run without holding a key [4]:

`cl_alwaysrun 1`

With it on, forward and back speeds are doubled while side speed stays the same, and movement is still clamped to `sv_maxspeed` [4].

answers.question: Can I play with a gamepad or controller?
answers.answer:
Yes — controller support is enabled by default (`joy_enable` is `1`).

- To turn it off, type `joy_enable 0`; set it back with `joy_enable 1` [1].
- Adjust look speed with `joy_sensitivity_yaw` (default `240`) and `joy_sensitivity_pitch` (default `130`) [2][3].
- If your controller’s buttons are mapped wrong, run `gamecontrollerdb_reload` to refresh SDL mappings [4].
- If looking feels inverted, set `joy_invert 1` [3].

answers.question: How do I connect to a multiplayer server?
answers.answer:
Open the console and type `connect` followed by the server’s IP address, DNS hostname, or local server name [1]. The default port is 26000; if the server uses a different port, set the `port` variable to that number before connecting [1].

- To find local servers, use `slist`; it broadcasts on the local network and lists servers you can then connect to by name [2].
- To reconnect to the last server, use `connect last` [1].
- Press Tab after `connect` to autocomplete from server history [1].
- If you get disconnected, `reconnect` quickly reconnects to the last network server [3].
- To leave a server, use `disconnect` [4].

Connection retries are controlled by `net_connectattempts`, default `3` [5]. The handshake timeout is `net_connecttimeout`, default `10` seconds [6]. `net_connectsearch` defaults to `1`; set it to `0` to skip the local host search before connecting [7].

answers.question: How do I set my player name and colors?
answers.answer:
Type `name` in the console to set your player name — with no argument it opens the name for editing, which is handy for names with special characters [1]. The name defaults to `player` [2].

For colors, use the `color` command [3]:

- `color 4` sets both shirt and pants to red.
- `color 4 13` sets shirt red and pants blue.
- `color x x` picks random colors for both [3].

Colors range from 0 to 13; anything above that just renders blue [3]. The traditional values are 0 white, 1 brown, 2 light blue, 3 green, 4 red, 5 orange, 6 gold, 7 peach, 8 purple, 9 magenta, 10 tan, 11 green, 12 yellow, 13 blue [4]. Hex RGB works too, e.g. `color 0xff00ff 0x00ff00` [3]. Typing `color` alone reports your current shirt and pants colors [3].

answers.question: How do I check my connection and make online play feel smoother?
answers.answer:
Use `scr_ping` to check your connection. The default `scr_ping 1` shows ping; set `scr_ping 3` to also show packet-loss text in the lower-left, updated every 5 seconds [1]. For more detail, run `net_stats` and watch packetsReSent, receivedDuplicateCount, shortPacketCount, and droppedDatagrams — high values mean a poor connection or server route [2].

For smoother online play:

- Keep clientside prediction on with `cl_nopred 0` (default) [3].
- Keep entity motion smooth with `cl_nolerp 0` (default), so objects do not jump between points [4].
- If many players cause slowdown, `gl_playermip 2` shrinks player-model textures [5].
- `host_maxfps` caps FPS; default is `250`. Use `host_maxfps 0` to uncap it [6].

answers.question: How do I chat, team chat, and mute other players?
answers.answer:
To chat to everyone, type `say <message>`, or run `messagemode` to open the text line; press Enter to send, Escape to cancel [1][2]. For team-only chat, use `say_team <message>` or `messagemode2` [3][4]. `messagemode2` is not bound by default [4]. To send plain console lines as chat, set `cl_chatmode 1` (default `0`); value `2` adds a leading space so commands, cvars, and aliases aren’t triggered [5].

To mute a player’s text chat, type `ignore <name>` while connected; `ignore` alone lists ignored players, and `unignore <name>` restores them. Partial names work, and the list clears when you disconnect [6][7]. To mute voice chat, use `vignore <slot> 1`; `vignore <slot> 0` unmutes, and `unmuteall` unmutes everyone you vignore’d [8][9]. The `mute` command only toggles your own volume [10].

answers.question: How do I host my own server?
answers.answer:
Run the engine with `-dedicated` to start a dedicated server; it stays in text mode and defaults to 16 players, the maximum allowed [1]. A listen server is started with `-listen 16` instead, but running one as a public server isn't recommended [2].

Then set it up from the console:

- `hostname "My Server"` — the name other players see [3]
- `deathmatch 3` — recommended for a public server, so weapons don't disappear [4]
- `maxplayers 16` — cap the player count [2]
- `password "secret"` — optional, to require a password [5]
- `rcon_password "secret"` — optional, for remote admin [5]

Use `-port <n>` if you need a port other than the default 26000 [6].

answers.question: How do I record and play back demos?
answers.answer:
To record, type `record` in the console. With no arguments it saves to `id1/demos`, using the map name and date as the filename [1]. Type `stop` to end recording; the demo is then written to disk [2]. The recording format is set by `cl_demo_format`, default `dem`; supported builds also accept `dz` for compressed DZip archives [3]. For automatic recording, `cl_autodemo` defaults to `0`; set it to `1` to record every new map, `2` for official CRMOD/CRCTF matches only, `3` for online only, or `4` to split at map changes [4].

To play a demo, use `playdemo <name>` [5]; stop it with `stopdemo` [6]. To queue several demos, use `startdemos e1m1 dm3 quad` (up to 32, no `.dem` extension needed) [7]. `cl_demoreel` defaults to `1`, so queued demos play in sequence; if set to `0`, `startdemos` opens the menu instead [7][8]. `demos` plays demos queued with `startdemos` [9].

answers.question: How do I take screenshots, and where are they saved?
answers.answer:
Type `screenshot` in the console to grab the current screen. You can pick a format and quality: `screenshot png`, `screenshot jpg 100`, or `screenshot tga` — supported formats are tga, png, and jpg, with quality from 1 to 100 [1].

Shots are written to the `screenshots` folder inside your game directory, named like `qssm_<timestamp>.png` or `qssm_<map>_<timestamp>.png` when you're in a map [2].

To view them, run `open screenshots` in the console, which opens that folder in your system's file browser [3].

You can also bind the command to a key, for example `bind F12 "screenshot jpg 100"`, so a single press captures a shot [1].

answers.question: How do I change volume and music?
answers.answer:
Set overall game volume with `volume` (default `0.7`); it controls music and sound effects [1]. Background CD music has its own `bgmvolume` (default `1`) [2], and ambient sounds use `ambient_level` (default `0.3`) [3].

For external music, `bgm_extmusic` is on by default (`1`) [4]. Put tracks in `Quake/id1/music` named `track02.ogg`, `track03.ogg`, etc. — there is no track01 — then use `music` to play one; MP3, OGG, FLAC and other formats work, and you can omit the extension [5]. Launch with `-noextmusic` to disable external music [6].

Playback controls: `music_pause`, `music_resume`, `music_stop`, `music_loop`, and `music_jump` (module music only) [7][8][9][10][11]. `music_preview` plays a file without replacing gameplay music [12].

answers.question: QSS-M won't start or crashes. What should I try?
answers.answer:
If QSS-M fails to launch, the usual culprits are sound or video initialization.

- Start with sound disabled: launch with `-nosound` [1]. You can also set `nosound 1` in the console, though it only fully silences everything after a restart or map change [2].
- For video problems, run `vid_restart`, which re-applies `vid_width`, `vid_height`, `vid_fullscreen`, `vid_refreshrate`, and `vid_bpp` [3]. If you're stuck in a bad fullscreen mode, try `vid_bpp 16` (the default; 16 or 32 are the valid values) and then `vid_restart` [4].
- To capture what happens before a crash, launch with `-condebug` to write a log to `qconsole.log` [5]. You can cap the log size in MiB, e.g. `-condebug 5` [6]. Once running, `condump` writes the console buffer to `condump.txt` [7].

answers.question: Why does the game stutter or the sound crackle?
answers.answer:
Sound crackle usually means your framerate is dropping below what the sound buffer covers. With `_snd_mixahead` at its default `0.1`, anything under 10 fps runs off the end of the mixed buffer and you hear stuttering [1]. Raise it, e.g. `_snd_mixahead 0.2`, which holds down to 5 fps — but higher values make the CPU mix more sound, which can itself lower your framerate [1].

For general hitching, check your frame cap: `host_maxfps` defaults to `250`, and `host_maxfps 0` uncaps it [2]. A negative value renders uncapped while fixing the network packet rate, e.g. `host_maxfps -100` for 100 packets per second [2]. Vertical sync also caps you at your monitor's refresh rate; `vid_vsync 1` enables it and `0` disables it, which is the default [3].

If a single sound is stuck looping, `stopsound` halts all playback [4].

answers.question: How do I find a setting when I don't know its name?
answers.answer:
If you don't know the exact name, search for a fragment of it.

- `apropos <text>` searches command and cvar names for the given substring [1].
- `find <text>` does the same thing [2].
- `cmdlist` prints an alphabetized list of all commands; add a substring to list only commands that start with it [3].
- `cvarlist` prints an alphabetized list of all console variables; add a substring to list only cvars that start with it [4].

For example, if you remember a setting has "name" in it, try `apropos name` or `find name`. If you know how it starts, `cvarlist cl_` narrows the list to cvars beginning with `cl_`.
